input.summary:
Guest bath lamplighting is written but blocked: parts/room-7.mjs now places three hanging lanterns at x36 z55/57/59 (y9), which a scratch copy shows lifts all 21 floor cells to 8+ with walk and fit OK. In the real build every lantern is refused because the mansion shell owns the room's air, so the room is still 21/21 dark.
Make.sh produces build.nbt, but the room has no furniture and the lamps do not land. The unlock belongs to the shell and room designer, not to this part; I did not bypass the lock.
left: Blocked: the mansion shell (parts/shell.mjs) carves and owns every guest bath air cell, so runParts refuses all writes there (lanterns refused 3 of 3 at 36,9,55/57/59). Until room air is left unlocked, the room stays at light 0 on all 21 floor cells.

The room designer's furniture (3-cell water_cauldron tub, planks vanity with basin cauldron and flower pot, linen barrel) is not built at all: parts/room-7.mjs build() was empty and its layout is only in comments, so the focal piece is absent. Same lock cause.

Verified on a scratch copy of build.nbt (not the real build): three hanging lanterns at (36,9,55), (36,9,57), (36,9,59) give min light 8, 0 dark, walk 21/21 reachable, fit OK. A single standing lantern at (35,4,55) also reaches 8+, but it sits on the west lane the designer kept clear, so I chose the hanging set.

parts/room-7.mjs now has an added import of B from the build library and the three lantern calls at the end of build(g). Each build logs these as 3 refusals for guest bath until the shell unlocks the room.

waste.what: Testing lantern spots by hand: I wrote a scratch node script that loads build.nbt, places candidate lanterns, saves a copy and runs mcd room on it, then compared the light grids for each candidate.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and one throwaway script in /tmp; the real build could not be used because every write was refused
waste.tool: mcd room should accept candidate lantern spots as a flag (e.g. --try x,y,z,hanging) and simulate them on a copy without writing, and report the candidate's min light and whether it passes the walk and fit checks

waste.what: Working out why the lanterns did nothing: the room check printed dark cells and a lamp suggestion without saying the writes were refused by the shell's ownership lock. I had to read parts-report.json and runParts' owned-set code to find it.
waste.cost: 2 extra greps and one parts-report read, plus one rebuild to confirm
waste.tool: mcd room (and mcd light) should flag when the room's air is owned by an earlier part, e.g. 'room air locked by shell: lamp writes refused', and list the refusals from parts-report.json for that room

waste.what: Lamp suggestion ignored the designer's lane: the room tool's best single spot (standing lantern at 35,4,55) is on the x35 lane the designer marked clear, and the tool does not read the lane comments.
waste.cost: one judgement call, then a scratch test to find an alternative that also reaches 8+
waste.tool: mcd room could take lane or keep-clear cells from the room designer's header comment or a rooms.json field, and filter lamp spots that would block them

companions.task: Leave the guest bath's air (x35..37, z54..60, y4..9) unowned in parts/shell.mjs, or let room parts own it, so the room designer's furniture and my three hanging lanterns can land. Then confirm build.nbt's parts-report shows no refusals for guest bath.

Build the guest bath's tub, vanity and linen barrel from the commented layout in parts/room-7.mjs once the room is unlocked. Then re-run the room check: the tub is the focal piece and must be in the light.
